Shri Greeshm Jain - Advocate for respondent Nos. 1 & 
 Order
This is a petition by the petitioner seeking quashment of order dated 4.8.2025 (Annexure P-1) by which the employment to the petitioner has been declined.
2 . The facts of the case, in short, are that a land owned by the petitioner and his family, was acquired by respondents/Northern Coalfields Limited.

As the compensation was not being paid upon acquisition, the petitioner's family approached the Part Time Tribunal Coal Bearing Areas Acquisition/Development Act, 1957 (hereinafter referred to as the Tribunal).

entities.text: Part Time Tribunal Coal Bearing Areas Acquisition/Development Act, 1957
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The Tribunal vide award dated 6.12.2022 (Annexure P-4) held the mother of the petitioner entitled for compensation upon acquisition of land belonging to her.
The award dated 6.12.2022 (Annexure P-4) was assailed by the respondents by way of filing a Miscellaneous Appeal before this Court vide M.A. No.2017 of 2023.

The said appeal was also dismissed by this Court NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-JBP:26766 2 WP-34700-2025 vide order dated 23.11.2023 (Annexure P-5).

After dismissal of the appeal, the compensation was paid to the family of the petitioner and the mother of the petitioner had moved an application and also executed an affidavit dated 7.5.2024 (Annexure P-8) seeking employment in favour of the petitioner.
However, the employment has been declined to the petitioner vide impugned order dated 4.8.2025 (Annexure P-1).
Hence, this petition.

1 3.
It is contended by the counsel for the petitioner that the impugned order has been passed in a purely arbitrary and callous manner.

The respondents while making reference to the provisions of the Policy have declined employment to the petitioner on the ground that the petitioner's name was not recorded as owner of the property at the time of acquisition.
On the contrary, at the time of acquisition, the name of State Government was recorded as owner.
The Authority further observed in the impugned order that as the employment was being sought after 33 years from the date of acquisition of land, the benefit of employment cannot be extended.

It is further contended that once the Tribunal has found the mother of the petitioner entitled for compensation and name of the petitioner's family was also subsequently recorded in the revenue record upon correction, there was no impediment in granting employment to the petitioner.

4. Per contra, the counsel for the respondents has contended that when the order passed by the Tribunal was assailed before this Court in Misc. Appeal No. 2017 of 2023, this Court in unequivocal term observed that the Tribunal had not determined the title but had only determined the eligibility of the claimant to claim compensation on the basis of reinstatement of his NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:26766 3 WP-34700-2025 title in the revenue records and accordingly,
dismissed the appeal.
Therefore, it is apparent that the question of title was never decided by any competent Court of law.

This Court affirmed the decision of the Tribunal pertaining to entitlement of compensation to the petitioner's family, that does not ip so facto makes the claimant owner of the property as there cannot be any direction by the Tribunal to confer benefit of title of the property.
Therefore, the petitioner was not entitled for employment.

The counsel for the respondents has placed reliance on the decision of Division Bench of this Court in Writ Appeal No. 254 of 2023 (Dinesh Kumar Lahre Vs. The State of M.P. & others) and other connected matters decided on 9.5.2025 to submit that right of employment in lieu of acquisition of land is not a fundamental right nor it can be claimed as such as a matter of right.

sentences.text:
5. Heard submissions and perused the record.
6 .

On perusal of record, it reflects that the Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy of Coal India Limited, 2012 (hereinafter referred to as the Policy of 2012) contained the definition of "land owner", the same is reproduced as under:-
"4. Definitions (a) xxxxxxxxxx (b) xxxxxxxxx (c) "land owner" includes any person- (i) whose name is recorded as the owner of the land or part thereof in the records of the concerned authority or NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:26766 4 WP-34700-2025 Sanjay Gupta vs The Ncl Through Its Chief Managing ... on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/159580284/
2 (ii) who is entitled to be granted Patta rights on the land under any law of the State including assigned lands or (iii) who has been declared as such by an order of the court or District Collector."
7.

entities.text: Rehabilitation and Resettlement Policy of Coal India Limited, 2012
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: A perusal of aforesaid reflects that for the purpose of extension of benefit of compensation as well as employment, the person, whose name is recorded as the owner of land in the revenue records of the concerned Authority, shall be treated to be the land owner.
It is further mentioned in the aforesaid definition that if a person who has been declared as such by an order of the Court of District Collector, shall also treated to be the land owner.
In the case in hand, the mother of the petitioner was found entitled for the compensation by the order of the Tribunal.

Indisputably,
subsequently, the name of the mother of the petitioner was also recorded in the revenue records as the owner.

It is also evident from perusal of order dated 23.11.2023 passed by this Court in M.A. No.
2017 of 2023 that from the year 1958-59 till the year 1986-87, the name of ancestors of the petitioner were recorded in the revenue records and subsequently, the land was recorded in the name of the State Government.
However, again the land was recorded in the name of the mother of the petitioner.

Therefore, in the case in hand, clause 4(c) of the Policy of 2012 which contained the definition of the "land owner" was required to be taken note of by the respondents while passing the impugned order.

It is also undisputed that the compensation in terms of the order of the Tribunal has also been paid to the petitioner and the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-JBP:26766 5 WP-34700-2025 said order has attained the finality and there is subsequent mutation in the revenue record in the name of mother of the petitioner, therefore, the matter requires reconsideration by the respondents.
8. The decision relied upon by the counsel for the respondent is of no assistance considering the peculiar facts of the present case.
9. Accordingly, the petition is allowed .
Impugned order dated 4.8.2025 (Annexure P-1) stands set aside.

The matter is remitted back to the respondents to take decision on the claim of the petitioner afresh taking into consideration the definition of "land owner" contained in Clause 4(c)(iii) of the Policy of 2012.
1 0 . Let a decision afresh be taken, in terms of this order, by the Authority concerned, within a period of 60 days from the date of production of certified copy of this order.
11. The petitioner shall be at liberty to produce all the documents in support of his claim before the Authority including mutation of name of the mother of the petitioner in the revenue record.
